प्रत्येक पद हे त्याच्या आधीच्या दोन पदांची बेरीज आहे — म्हणजे फिबोनाची प्रकारचा नमुना.
पुढचे पद = 39 + 63 = 102.
एखाद्या श्रेणीची गुणोत्तरे हळूहळू सुमारे 1.6 कडे सरकत असतील, तर लगेच या नमुन्याचा संशय घ्यावा.

en.text: Find the next term in the series: 7, 6, 13, 16, 19, 26, ?
en.explanation:
The terms rise and fall irregularly, which is the signature of TWO series woven together. Split them by position.
Terms in the 1st, 3rd and 5th positions: 7, 13, 19 — each is 6 more than the one before.
Terms in the 2nd, 4th and 6th positions: 6, 16, 26 — each is 10 more than the one before.
The missing term sits in the 7th position, so it belongs to the FIRST series.
It follows 19, so it equals 19 + 6 = 25.
When a series zig-zags, always try separating the odd-numbered and even-numbered positions before anything else.

mr.explanation:
पदे अनियमितपणे वरखाली होत आहेत, हे दोन श्रेणी एकमेकांत गुंफल्याचे लक्षण आहे. स्थानानुसार त्या वेगळ्या करा.
1, 3 व 5 व्या स्थानांवरील पदे: 7, 13, 19 — प्रत्येक आधीच्यापेक्षा 6 ने मोठे.
2, 4 व 6 व्या स्थानांवरील पदे: 6, 16, 26 — प्रत्येक आधीच्यापेक्षा 10 ने मोठे.
हरवलेले पद 7 व्या स्थानी आहे, म्हणून ते पहिल्या श्रेणीतील आहे.
ते 19 नंतर येते, म्हणून ते 19 + 6 = 25 इतके आहे.
श्रेणी वरखाली होत असेल, तर इतर काहीही करण्यापूर्वी विषम व सम स्थाने वेगळी करून पाहावीत.

en.text: Find the next term in the series: 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, ?
en.explanation:
Start by taking the differences between consecutive terms.
13 − 7 = 6, 19 − 13 = 6, 25 − 19 = 6, 31 − 25 = 6.
The difference is constant at 6, so this is an arithmetic series.
The next term = 31 + 6 = 37.
Always compute the differences first — if they come out constant, the series is settled in seconds and you can move on.

mr.explanation:
प्रथम लागोपाठच्या पदांतील फरक काढा.
13 − 7 = 6, 19 − 13 = 6, 25 − 19 = 6, 31 − 25 = 6.
फरक सर्वत्र 6 असा स्थिर आहे, म्हणून ही अंकगणिती श्रेणी आहे.
पुढचे पद = 31 + 6 = 37.
नेहमी आधी फरक काढावेत — ते स्थिर आले की श्रेणी क्षणात सुटते आणि वेळ वाचतो.

en.text: Find the next term in the series: 6, 9, 17, 30, 48, ?
en.explanation:
The differences between consecutive terms are 3, 8, 13, 18 — not constant, so look one level deeper.
The differences OF those differences are 5, 5, 5 — constant.
So the gaps themselves grow by 5 each time.
The next gap = 18 + 5 = 23.
The next term = 48 + 23 = 71.
When the first differences are not constant, take the second differences before abandoning the idea — a great many exam series are of exactly this type.

mr.explanation:
लागोपाठच्या पदांतील फरक 3, 8, 13, 18 असे आहेत — ते स्थिर नाहीत, म्हणून आणखी एक पायरी खोल पाहा.
या फरकांचे फरक 5, 5, 5 असे स्थिर आहेत.
म्हणजे प्रत्येक वेळी अंतर 5 ने वाढते.
पुढचे अंतर = 18 + 5 = 23.
पुढचे पद = 48 + 23 = 71.
पहिले फरक स्थिर नसतील तर लगेच हार न मानता दुसरे फरक काढावेत — परीक्षेतील पुष्कळ श्रेणी नेमक्या याच प्रकारच्या असतात.

en.text: Find the next term in the series: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, ?
en.explanation:
The differences (2, 4, 8, 16) are not constant, and neither are the ratios, so test a two-step rule of the form "multiply, then add".
Try multiplying by 2 and then subtract 1:
3 × 2 − 1 = 5 ✓
5 × 2 − 1 = 9 ✓
9 × 2 − 1 = 17 ✓
17 × 2 − 1 = 33 ✓
The rule holds throughout, so the next term = 33 × 2 − 1 = 65.
When neither differences nor ratios work, a combined multiply-and-add rule is the next thing to try.

mr.text: पुढील श्रेणीतील पुढचे पद कोणते: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, ?
mr.explanation:
फरक (2, 4, 8, 16) स्थिर नाहीत आणि गुणोत्तरेही स्थिर नाहीत, म्हणून "गुणा आणि मग मिळवा" अशा दोन पायऱ्यांच्या नियमाची चाचणी घ्या.
2 ने गुणून नंतर 1 वजा करा:
3 × 2 − 1 = 5 ✓
5 × 2 − 1 = 9 ✓
9 × 2 − 1 = 17 ✓
17 × 2 − 1 = 33 ✓
नियम सर्वत्र लागू होतो, म्हणून पुढचे पद = 33 × 2 − 1 = 65.
फरक व गुणोत्तर दोन्ही चालत नसतील, तेव्हा गुणाकार-अधिक-बेरीज हा एकत्रित नियम तपासावा.

en.text: Find the next term in the series: 37, 50, 65, 82, 101, ?
en.explanation:
The terms grow too fast for a constant difference, so compare them against the squares of small whole numbers.
6² = 36, and 36 plus 1 = 37
7² = 49, and 49 plus 1 = 50
8² = 64, and 64 plus 1 = 65
9² = 81, and 81 plus 1 = 82
10² = 100, and 100 plus 1 = 101
So each term is the square of 6, 7, 8, ... taken in order plus 1.
The next base is 11, so the next term = 11² plus 1 = 121 + 1 = 122.
Keeping the squares up to 30 and the cubes up to 15 in memory turns these questions into instant marks.

mr.explanation:
पदे इतक्या वेगाने वाढतात की स्थिर फरक शक्य नाही, म्हणून लहान संख्यांच्या वर्गांशी तुलना करा.
6² = 36, आणि 36 अधिक 1 = 37
7² = 49, आणि 49 अधिक 1 = 50
8² = 64, आणि 64 अधिक 1 = 65
9² = 81, आणि 81 अधिक 1 = 82
10² = 100, आणि 100 अधिक 1 = 101
म्हणजे प्रत्येक पद हे 6, 7, 8, ... यांचा क्रमवार वर्ग अधिक 1 आहे.
पुढचा आधार 11 आहे, म्हणून पुढचे पद = 11² अधिक 1 = 121 + 1 = 122.
30 पर्यंतचे वर्ग व 15 पर्यंतचे घन पाठ असतील तर असे प्रश्न क्षणात सुटतात.

en.text: Find the next term in the series: 1, 7, 8, 15, 23, 38, ?
en.explanation:
The differences are not constant and the ratios drift, so try adding pairs of earlier terms.
1 + 7 = 8 ✓
7 + 8 = 15 ✓
8 + 15 = 23 ✓
15 + 23 = 38 ✓
Every term is the sum of the two terms immediately before it — a Fibonacci-style pattern.
The next term = 23 + 38 = 61.
Whenever the ratios of a series creep slowly towards about 1.6, suspect this pattern straight away.

mr.explanation:
फरक स्थिर नाहीत आणि गुणोत्तरेही हळूहळू बदलतात, म्हणून आधीच्या पदांच्या जोड्या मिळवून पाहा.
1 + 7 = 8 ✓
7 + 8 = 15 ✓
8 + 15 = 23 ✓
15 + 23 = 38 ✓
प्रत्येक पद हे त्याच्या आधीच्या दोन पदांची बेरीज आहे — म्हणजे फिबोनाची प्रकारचा नमुना.
पुढचे पद = 23 + 38 = 61.
एखाद्या श्रेणीची गुणोत्तरे हळूहळू सुमारे 1.6 कडे सरकत असतील, तर लगेच या नमुन्याचा संशय घ्यावा.

en.text: Find the next term in the series: 9, 2, 13, 11, 17, 20, ?
en.explanation:
The terms rise and fall irregularly, which is the signature of TWO series woven together. Split them by position.
Terms in the 1st, 3rd and 5th positions: 9, 13, 17 — each is 4 more than the one before.
Terms in the 2nd, 4th and 6th positions: 2, 11, 20 — each is 9 more than the one before.
The missing term sits in the 7th position, so it belongs to the FIRST series.
It follows 17, so it equals 17 + 4 = 21.
When a series zig-zags, always try separating the odd-numbered and even-numbered positions before anything else.

mr.explanation:
पदे अनियमितपणे वरखाली होत आहेत, हे दोन श्रेणी एकमेकांत गुंफल्याचे लक्षण आहे. स्थानानुसार त्या वेगळ्या करा.
1, 3 व 5 व्या स्थानांवरील पदे: 9, 13, 17 — प्रत्येक आधीच्यापेक्षा 4 ने मोठे.
2, 4 व 6 व्या स्थानांवरील पदे: 2, 11, 20 — प्रत्येक आधीच्यापेक्षा 9 ने मोठे.
हरवलेले पद 7 व्या स्थानी आहे, म्हणून ते पहिल्या श्रेणीतील आहे.
ते 17 नंतर येते, म्हणून ते 17 + 4 = 21 इतके आहे.
श्रेणी वरखाली होत असेल, तर इतर काहीही करण्यापूर्वी विषम व सम स्थाने वेगळी करून पाहावीत.

en.text: In a certain code language, LADDER is written as QFIIJW. How will TEMPLE be written in the same code?
en.explanation:
Line up the given word against its code, letter by letter:
L → Q, A → F, D → I, D → I, E → J, R → W.
Each letter has moved 5 places forward in the alphabet, and the same shift applies to every letter of the word.
Now apply exactly the same rule to TEMPLE:
T → Y, E → J, M → R, P → U, L → Q, E → J.
So TEMPLE is written as YJRUQJ.
Check the direction carefully — shifting 5 the other way would give OZHKGZ, which is offered as a distractor.

mr.text: एका सांकेतिक भाषेत LADDER हा शब्द QFIIJW असा लिहितात. तर त्याच संकेतानुसार TEMPLE हा शब्द कसा लिहिला जाईल?
mr.explanation:
दिलेला शब्द व त्याचा संकेत अक्षरशः एकाखाली एक मांडा:
L → Q, A → F, D → I, D → I, E → J, R → W.
प्रत्येक अक्षर वर्णमालेत 5 स्थाने पुढे सरकले आहे, आणि हाच बदल शब्दातील प्रत्येक अक्षराला लागू होतो.
आता तोच नियम TEMPLE या शब्दाला लावा:
T → Y, E → J, M → R, P → U, L → Q, E → J.
म्हणून TEMPLE हा शब्द YJRUQJ असा लिहिला जाईल.
दिशा नीट तपासा — 5 स्थाने उलट दिशेने सरकवल्यास OZHKGZ येते, जो पर्यायांत सापळा म्हणून दिला आहे.

en.text: In a certain code language, NUMBER is written as REBMUN. How will TEMPLE be written in the same code?
en.explanation:
Line up the given word against its code, letter by letter:
N → R, U → E, M → B, B → M, E → U, R → N.
No letter has changed — only the ORDER has. The code is simply the word written backwards, with the first letter becoming the last.
Now apply exactly the same rule to TEMPLE:
T → E, E → L, M → P, P → M, L → E, E → T.
So TEMPLE is written as ELPMET.
Before hunting for an alphabet shift, always check whether the code uses exactly the same set of letters — if it does, the rule is about order, not substitution.

mr.text: एका सांकेतिक भाषेत NUMBER हा शब्द REBMUN असा लिहितात. तर त्याच संकेतानुसार TEMPLE हा शब्द कसा लिहिला जाईल?
mr.explanation:
दिलेला शब्द व त्याचा संकेत अक्षरशः एकाखाली एक मांडा:
N → R, U → E, M → B, B → M, E → U, R → N.
कोणतेही अक्षर बदललेले नाही — फक्त क्रम बदलला आहे. संकेत म्हणजे तोच शब्द उलट्या क्रमाने लिहिलेला, पहिले अक्षर शेवटी जाते.
आता तोच नियम TEMPLE या शब्दाला लावा:
T → E, E → L, M → P, P → M, L → E, E → T.
म्हणून TEMPLE हा शब्द ELPMET असा लिहिला जाईल.
वर्णमालेतील सरकाव शोधण्यापूर्वी संकेतात तीच अक्षरे आहेत का ते तपासा — तशी असतील तर नियम क्रमाचा असतो, अक्षरबदलाचा नाही.

en.text: In a certain code language, MARKET is written as NCUOJZ. How will NUMBER be written in the same code?
en.explanation:
Line up the given word against its code, letter by letter:
M → N, A → C, R → U, K → O, E → J, T → Z.
The shift is not the same throughout. The 1st letter moves 1 place forward, the 2nd moves 2 places, the 3rd moves 3, and so on — the shift equals the position of the letter.
Now apply exactly the same rule to NUMBER:
N → O, U → W, M → P, B → F, E → J, R → X.
So NUMBER is written as OWPFJX.
Whenever the first two letters shift by different amounts, stop looking for a fixed shift and check whether the shift is tracking the letter's position.

mr.text: एका सांकेतिक भाषेत MARKET हा शब्द NCUOJZ असा लिहितात. तर त्याच संकेतानुसार NUMBER हा शब्द कसा लिहिला जाईल?
mr.explanation:
दिलेला शब्द व त्याचा संकेत अक्षरशः एकाखाली एक मांडा:
M → N, A → C, R → U, K → O, E → J, T → Z.
सरकाव सर्वत्र सारखा नाही. पहिले अक्षर 1 स्थान पुढे, दुसरे 2 स्थाने, तिसरे 3 स्थाने असे सरकते — म्हणजे सरकाव त्या अक्षराच्या स्थानाइतका असतो.
आता तोच नियम NUMBER या शब्दाला लावा:
N → O, U → W, M → P, B → F, E → J, R → X.
म्हणून NUMBER हा शब्द OWPFJX असा लिहिला जाईल.
पहिली दोन अक्षरे वेगवेगळ्या प्रमाणात सरकत असतील, तर स्थिर सरकाव शोधणे थांबवा आणि सरकाव अक्षराच्या स्थानाबरोबर वाढतो का ते तपासा.

en.text: In a certain code language, WINTER is written as YGPRGP. How will JACKET be written in the same code?
en.explanation:
Line up the given word against its code, letter by letter:
W → Y, I → G, N → P, T → R, E → G, R → P.
The letters in the odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th) move 2 places forward, while the letters in the even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th) move 2 places backward.
Now apply exactly the same rule to JACKET:
J → L, A → Y, C → E, K → I, E → G, T → R.
So JACKET is written as LYEIGR.
Applying the same forward shift to every letter would give LCEMGV — the alternating direction is the whole point of this pattern.

mr.text: एका सांकेतिक भाषेत WINTER हा शब्द YGPRGP असा लिहितात. तर त्याच संकेतानुसार JACKET हा शब्द कसा लिहिला जाईल?
mr.explanation:
दिलेला शब्द व त्याचा संकेत अक्षरशः एकाखाली एक मांडा:
W → Y, I → G, N → P, T → R, E → G, R → P.
विषम स्थानांवरील अक्षरे (1 ले, 3 रे, 5 वे) 2 स्थाने पुढे सरकतात, तर सम स्थानांवरील अक्षरे (2 रे, 4 थे, 6 वे) 2 स्थाने मागे सरकतात.
आता तोच नियम JACKET या शब्दाला लावा:
J → L, A → Y, C → E, K → I, E → G, T → R.
म्हणून JACKET हा शब्द LYEIGR असा लिहिला जाईल.
प्रत्येक अक्षराला एकाच दिशेने सरकाव दिल्यास LCEMGV येते — आलटून पालटून बदलणारी दिशा हाच या नमुन्याचा गाभा आहे.

en.text: In a certain code language, DOCTOR is written as FQEVQT. How will MASTER be written in the same code?
en.explanation:
Line up the given word against its code, letter by letter:
D → F, O → Q, C → E, T → V, O → Q, R → T.
Each letter has moved 2 places forward in the alphabet, and the same shift applies to every letter of the word.
Now apply exactly the same rule to MASTER:
M → O, A → C, S → U, T → V, E → G, R → T.
So MASTER is written as OCUVGT.
Check the direction carefully — shifting 2 the other way would give KYQRCP, which is offered as a distractor.

mr.explanation:
दिलेला शब्द व त्याचा संकेत अक्षरशः एकाखाली एक मांडा:

प्रत्येक अक्षर वर्णमालेत 2 स्थाने पुढे सरकले आहे, आणि हाच बदल शब्दातील प्रत्येक अक्षराला लागू होतो.
आता तोच नियम MASTER या शब्दाला लावा:

म्हणून MASTER हा शब्द OCUVGT असा लिहिला जाईल.
दिशा नीट तपासा — 2 स्थाने उलट दिशेने सरकवल्यास KYQRCP येते, जो पर्यायांत सापळा म्हणून दिला आहे.

en.text: In a certain code language, MASTER is written as NZHGVI. How will CIRCLE be written in the same code?
en.explanation:
Line up the given word against its code, letter by letter:
M → N, A → Z, S → H, T → G, E → V, R → I.
Each letter has been replaced by its OPPOSITE in the alphabet: A pairs with Z, B with Y, C with X and so on. The two positions in any pair always add up to 27.
Now apply exactly the same rule to CIRCLE:
C → X, I → R, R → I, C → X, L → O, E → V.
So CIRCLE is written as XRIXOV.
The quickest way to apply this rule is to remember the pairs A-Z, B-Y, C-X, D-W, E-V and M-N; the rest follow by counting from the nearer end.

mr.text: एका सांकेतिक भाषेत MASTER हा शब्द NZHGVI असा लिहितात. तर त्याच संकेतानुसार CIRCLE हा शब्द कसा लिहिला जाईल?
mr.explanation:

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 8 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. He then turns to his right and walks 5 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?
en.explanation:
Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 8 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 5 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 8 − 5 = 3 km.
On the other axis he has moved 4 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 3 km away in one direction and 4 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 km.
The total distance WALKED is 17 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

mr.text: एक माणूस प या ठिकाणाहून पूर्व दिशेला तोंड करून 8 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 4 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 5 किमी चालतो. तर आता तो प या ठिकाणापासून सरळ रेषेत किती किमी अंतरावर आहे?

संपूर्ण मार्ग एकदम डोळ्यासमोर आणण्यापेक्षा दोन्ही दिशा स्वतंत्रपणे मोजा.
तो प्रथम 8 किमी चालतो, नंतर दोन उजव्या वळणांनंतरचा 5 किमीचा शेवटचा टप्पा त्याला त्याच अक्षावर मागे आणतो, म्हणून त्या अक्षावरील निव्वळ प्रवास 8 − 5 = 3 किमी.
दुसऱ्या अक्षावर तो 4 किमी सरकला असून ते कशानेही रद्द होत नाही.
म्हणजे तो एका दिशेने 3 किमी व त्याला लंब दिशेने 4 किमी अंतरावर आहे — सरळ रेषेतील अंतर म्हणजे काटकोन त्रिकोणाचा कर्ण.
अंतर = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 किमी.
प्रत्यक्ष चाललेले एकूण अंतर 17 किमी आहे, पण प्रश्नात सरळ रेषेतील अंतर विचारले असून ते नेहमी कमीच असते.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 5 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. He then turns to his left and walks 6 km. He then turns to his left and walks 4 km. In which direction is he facing now?
en.explanation:
The distances are irrelevant here — only the turns change the direction he faces.
Start the compass at south.
Turning to his right from south makes him face west.
Turning to his left from west makes him face south.
Turning to his left from south makes him face east.

संपूर्ण मार्ग एकदम डोळ्यासमोर आणण्यापेक्षा दोन्ही दिशा स्वतंत्रपणे मोजा.
तो प्रथम 9 किमी चालतो, नंतर दोन उजव्या वळणांनंतरचा 3 किमीचा शेवटचा टप्पा त्याला त्याच अक्षावर मागे आणतो, म्हणून त्या अक्षावरील निव्वळ प्रवास 9 − 3 = 6 किमी.
दुसऱ्या अक्षावर तो 8 किमी सरकला असून ते कशानेही रद्द होत नाही.
म्हणजे तो एका दिशेने 6 किमी व त्याला लंब दिशेने 8 किमी अंतरावर आहे — सरळ रेषेतील अंतर म्हणजे काटकोन त्रिकोणाचा कर्ण.
अंतर = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 किमी.
प्रत्यक्ष चाललेले एकूण अंतर 20 किमी आहे, पण प्रश्नात सरळ रेषेतील अंतर विचारले असून ते नेहमी कमीच असते.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 5 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. He then turns to his right and walks 6 km. He then turns to his left and walks 4 km. In which direction is he facing now?
en.explanation:
The distances are irrelevant here — only the turns change the direction he faces.
Start the compass at south.
Turning to his right from south makes him face west.
Turning to his right from west makes him face north.
Turning to his left from north makes him face west.
So he is finally facing west.
Keep in mind that left and right are from the WALKER's point of view, so a right turn always moves the compass one quarter clockwise: north to east to south to west.

mr.text: एक माणूस प या ठिकाणाहून दक्षिण दिशेला तोंड करून 5 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 3 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 6 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या डाव्या बाजूला वळून 4 किमी चालतो. तर आता त्याचे तोंड कोणत्या दिशेला आहे?
mr.explanation:
येथे अंतरे बिनमहत्त्वाची आहेत — फक्त वळणांमुळेच तोंडाची दिशा बदलते.

दक्षिण कडून उजवीकडे वळल्यावर तोंड पश्चिम दिशेला होते.
पश्चिम कडून उजवीकडे वळल्यावर तोंड उत्तर दिशेला होते.
उत्तर कडून डावीकडे वळल्यावर तोंड पश्चिम दिशेला होते.
म्हणून शेवटी त्याचे तोंड पश्चिम दिशेला आहे.
डावे-उजवे हे चालणाऱ्याच्या दृष्टिकोनातून असते हे लक्षात ठेवा, म्हणून उजवे वळण होकायंत्र नेहमी एक चतुर्थांश घड्याळाच्या दिशेने फिरवते: उत्तर ते पूर्व ते दक्षिण ते पश्चिम.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces north, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 10 km takes him 10 km north along the north-south axis.
After turning to his right he is facing east, and the second leg of 3 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 10 km to the north and 3 km to the east of P.
When a point lies both to the north and to the east, its direction is north-east.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 6 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?
en.explanation:
Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 6 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 3 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 6 − 3 = 3 km.
On the other axis he has moved 4 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 3 km away in one direction and 4 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 km.
The total distance WALKED is 13 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces west, and walks 16 km. He then turns to his right and walks 16 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?
en.explanation:
Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 16 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 4 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 16 − 4 = 12 km.
On the other axis he has moved 16 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 12 km away in one direction and 16 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(12² + 16²) = √(144 + 256) = √400 = 20 km.
The total distance WALKED is 36 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

mr.text: एक माणूस प या ठिकाणाहून पश्चिम दिशेला तोंड करून 16 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 16 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 4 किमी चालतो. तर आता तो प या ठिकाणापासून सरळ रेषेत किती किमी अंतरावर आहे?

दुसऱ्या अक्षावर तो 16 किमी सरकला असून ते कशानेही रद्द होत नाही.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 5 km. He then turns to his left and walks 3 km. He then turns to his right and walks 6 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. In which direction is he facing now?
en.explanation:
The distances are irrelevant here — only the turns change the direction he faces.
Start the compass at east.
Turning to his left from east makes him face north.
Turning to his right from north makes him face east.
Turning to his right from east makes him face south.
So he is finally facing south.
Keep in mind that left and right are from the WALKER's point of view, so a right turn always moves the compass one quarter clockwise: north to east to south to west.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his right and walks 9 km. In which direction is he now from point P?

Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 10 km takes him 10 km south along the north-south axis.
After turning to his right he is facing west, and the second leg of 9 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 10 km to the south and 9 km to the west of P.
When a point lies both to the south and to the west, its direction is south-west.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 12 km. He then turns to his right and walks 15 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 6 km. He then turns to his left and walks 7 km. In which direction is he now from point P?

Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 6 km takes him 6 km east along the east-west axis.
After turning to his left he is facing north, and the second leg of 7 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 7 km to the north and 6 km to the east of P.

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 4 km. He then turns to his left and walks 9 km. In which direction is he now from point P?

Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 4 km takes him 4 km east along the east-west axis.
After turning to his left he is facing north, and the second leg of 9 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 9 km to the north and 4 km to the east of P.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces north, and walks 17 km. He then turns to his right and walks 16 km. He then turns to his right and walks 5 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 17 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 5 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 17 − 5 = 12 km.

The total distance WALKED is 38 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 13 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 4 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 13 − 4 = 9 km.
On the other axis he has moved 12 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 9 km away in one direction and 12 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(9² + 12²) = √(81 + 144) = √225 = 15 km.
The total distance WALKED is 29 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

mr.text: एक माणूस प या ठिकाणाहून उत्तर दिशेला तोंड करून 13 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 12 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 4 किमी चालतो. तर आता तो प या ठिकाणापासून सरळ रेषेत किती किमी अंतरावर आहे?

दुसऱ्या अक्षावर तो 12 किमी सरकला असून ते कशानेही रद्द होत नाही.
म्हणजे तो एका दिशेने 9 किमी व त्याला लंब दिशेने 12 किमी अंतरावर आहे — सरळ रेषेतील अंतर म्हणजे काटकोन त्रिकोणाचा कर्ण.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces north, and walks 5 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. He then turns to his left and walks 6 km. He then turns to his left and walks 4 km. In which direction is he facing now?
en.explanation:
The distances are irrelevant here — only the turns change the direction he faces.
Start the compass at north.
Turning to his right from north makes him face east.
Turning to his left from east makes him face north.
Turning to his left from north makes him face west.
So he is finally facing west.
Keep in mind that left and right are from the WALKER's point of view, so a right turn always moves the compass one quarter clockwise: north to east to south to west.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 6 km. He then turns to his left and walks 7 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 6 km takes him 6 km south along the north-south axis.
After turning to his left he is facing east, and the second leg of 7 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 6 km to the south and 7 km to the east of P.
When a point lies both to the south and to the east, its direction is south-east.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

दुसऱ्या अक्षावर तो 8 किमी सरकला असून ते कशानेही रद्द होत नाही.
म्हणजे तो एका दिशेने 6 किमी व त्याला लंब दिशेने 8 किमी अंतरावर आहे — सरळ रेषेतील अंतर म्हणजे काटकोन त्रिकोणाचा कर्ण.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces north, and walks 5 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. He then turns to his left and walks 6 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. In which direction is he facing now?
en.explanation:
The distances are irrelevant here — only the turns change the direction he faces.
Start the compass at north.
Turning to his right from north makes him face east.
Turning to his left from east makes him face north.
Turning to his right from north makes him face east.
So he is finally facing east.
Keep in mind that left and right are from the WALKER's point of view, so a right turn always moves the compass one quarter clockwise: north to east to south to west.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces west, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 10 km takes him 10 km west along the east-west axis.
After turning to his right he is facing north, and the second leg of 3 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 3 km to the north and 10 km to the west of P.
When a point lies both to the north and to the west, its direction is north-west.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 12 km. He then turns to his right and walks 12 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 12 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 3 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 12 − 3 = 9 km.
On the other axis he has moved 12 km, and nothing cancels it.

Distance = √(9² + 12²) = √(81 + 144) = √225 = 15 km.
The total distance WALKED is 27 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

दुसऱ्या अक्षावर तो 12 किमी सरकला असून ते कशानेही रद्द होत नाही.
म्हणजे तो एका दिशेने 9 किमी व त्याला लंब दिशेने 12 किमी अंतरावर आहे — सरळ रेषेतील अंतर म्हणजे काटकोन त्रिकोणाचा कर्ण.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 8 km. He then turns to his left and walks 7 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 8 km takes him 8 km south along the north-south axis.
After turning to his left he is facing east, and the second leg of 7 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 8 km to the south and 7 km to the east of P.
When a point lies both to the south and to the east, its direction is south-east.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 15 km. He then turns to his right and walks 16 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 15 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 3 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 15 − 3 = 12 km.
On the other axis he has moved 16 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 12 km away in one direction and 16 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(12² + 16²) = √(144 + 256) = √400 = 20 km.
The total distance WALKED is 34 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces north, and walks 4 km. He then turns to his right and walks 9 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 4 km takes him 4 km north along the north-south axis.
After turning to his right he is facing east, and the second leg of 9 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 4 km to the north and 9 km to the east of P.
When a point lies both to the north and to the east, its direction is north-east.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his right and walks 12 km. He then turns to his right and walks 5 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?

Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 10 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 5 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 10 − 5 = 5 km.
On the other axis he has moved 12 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 5 km away in one direction and 12 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 km.
The total distance WALKED is 27 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces west, and walks 8 km. He then turns to his left and walks 3 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces north, and walks 9 km. He then turns to his right and walks 12 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?

दुसऱ्या अक्षावर तो 8 किमी सरकला असून ते कशानेही रद्द होत नाही.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces east, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his left and walks 5 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 10 km takes him 10 km east along the east-west axis.
After turning to his left he is facing north, and the second leg of 5 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 5 km to the north and 10 km to the east of P.
When a point lies both to the north and to the east, its direction is north-east.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

mr.text: एक माणूस प या ठिकाणाहून पूर्व दिशेला तोंड करून 10 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या डाव्या बाजूला वळून 5 किमी चालतो. तर आता तो प या ठिकाणापासून कोणत्या दिशेला आहे?
mr.explanation:

एखादा बिंदू उत्तरेला व पूर्वेला अशा दोन्ही बाजूंना असेल, तेव्हा त्याची दिशा ईशान्य असते.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces west, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his right and walks 15 km. He then turns to his right and walks 2 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?
en.explanation:
Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 10 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 2 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 10 − 2 = 8 km.
On the other axis he has moved 15 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 8 km away in one direction and 15 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(8² + 15²) = √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17 km.
The total distance WALKED is 27 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his right and walks 3 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces west, and walks 10 km. He then turns to his right and walks 7 km. In which direction is he now from point P?
en.explanation:
Put point P at the origin and treat north as up and east as right.
His first leg of 10 km takes him 10 km west along the east-west axis.
After turning to his right he is facing north, and the second leg of 7 km moves him along the other axis.
Adding the two legs, he ends up 7 km to the north and 10 km to the west of P.
When a point lies both to the north and to the west, its direction is north-west.
The question asks where HE is relative to P, not where P is relative to him — those two are exact opposites, and mixing them up is the classic error.

mr.text: एक माणूस प या ठिकाणाहून पश्चिम दिशेला तोंड करून 10 किमी चालतो. नंतर तो आपल्या उजव्या बाजूला वळून 7 किमी चालतो. तर आता तो प या ठिकाणापासून कोणत्या दिशेला आहे?

प हे ठिकाण आरंभबिंदू धरा आणि उत्तर वर, पूर्व उजवीकडे असे मानून आकृती काढा.

en.text: A man starts from point P, faces south, and walks 9 km. He then turns to his right and walks 12 km. He then turns to his right and walks 4 km. How far, in km, is he now from point P in a straight line?
en.explanation:
Track the two directions separately rather than trying to picture the whole path at once.
He first walks 9 km, then after two right turns the last leg of 4 km takes him back along the same axis, so his net travel on that axis is 9 − 4 = 5 km.
On the other axis he has moved 12 km, and nothing cancels it.
So he is 5 km away in one direction and 12 km in a perpendicular direction — the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
Distance = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 km.
The total distance WALKED is 25 km, but the question asks for the straight-line gap, which is always smaller.

en.text: In a row of students, Rahul is 11th from the left end and 24th from the right end. How many students are there in the row?
en.explanation:
Being 11th from the left means there are 10 students to his left.
Being 24th from the right means there are 23 students to his right.
The row is everyone on his left, plus Rahul himself, plus everyone on his right:
Total = 10 + 1 + 23 = 34.
The usual shortcut is Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1, and the −1 is there because Rahul gets counted from both ends.
Simply adding the two positions gives 35, which counts him twice.

mr.text: एका रांगेत राहुल डाव्या टोकाकडून 11 वा आणि उजव्या टोकाकडून 24 वा आहे. तर रांगेत एकूण किती विद्यार्थी आहेत?
mr.explanation:
डावीकडून 11 वा असणे म्हणजे त्याच्या डावीकडे 10 विद्यार्थी आहेत.
उजवीकडून 24 वा असणे म्हणजे त्याच्या उजवीकडे 23 विद्यार्थी आहेत.
संपूर्ण रांग = डावीकडचे सर्व + स्वतः राहुल + उजवीकडचे सर्व:
एकूण = 10 + 1 + 23 = 34.
नेहमीचे सूत्र म्हणजे एकूण = (डावीकडून स्थान) + (उजवीकडून स्थान) − 1, आणि −1 अशासाठी की राहुल दोन्ही टोकांकडून मोजला जातो.
दोन्ही स्थाने नुसती मिळवल्यास 35 येते, ज्यात तो दोनदा मोजला जातो.

en.text: In a row of 32 students, Sita is 23th from the left end. What is her position from the right end?
en.explanation:
Being 23th from the left means 23 students have been counted up to and including Sita.
That leaves 32 − 23 = 9 students to her right.
Counting from the right end, those 9 students come first and Sita is the very next one.
So her position from the right = 9 + 1 = 10.
The formula is (position from right) = Total − (position from left) + 1. Stopping at 9 forgets to count Sita herself, and that off-by-one is what the question is testing.

mr.text: 32 विद्यार्थ्यांच्या रांगेत सीता डाव्या टोकाकडून 23 वी आहे. तर उजव्या टोकाकडून तिचे स्थान कितवे?
mr.explanation:
डावीकडून 23 वी असणे म्हणजे सीतेसह 23 विद्यार्थी मोजून झाले आहेत.
म्हणजे तिच्या उजवीकडे 32 − 23 = 9 विद्यार्थी उरतात.
उजव्या टोकाकडून मोजायला सुरुवात केल्यास ते 9 विद्यार्थी आधी येतात आणि लगेच सीता येते.
म्हणून उजवीकडून तिचे स्थान = 9 + 1 = 10.
सूत्र: (उजवीकडून स्थान) = एकूण − (डावीकडून स्थान) + 1. 9 वर थांबल्यास स्वतः सीता मोजायची राहून जाते, आणि हीच एका अंकाची चूक प्रश्नात तपासली जाते.

en.text: In a row of students, Karan is 7th from the left end and Meena is 9th from the right end. They interchange their positions, and Karan then becomes 21th from the left end. How many students are there in the row?
en.explanation:
The key idea is that swapping does not move anybody else — Karan simply steps into the exact spot Meena was standing in.
So Meena's original position from the left must have been 21.
We also know Meena was 9th from the right.
Applying the standard rule to Meena: Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1.
Total = 21 + 9 − 1 = 29.
Karan's original position of 7th is not needed at all — it is there to see whether you have understood which person the two facts now describe.

mr.text: एका रांगेत करण डाव्या टोकाकडून 7 वा आहे आणि मीना उजव्या टोकाकडून 9 वी आहे. दोघांनी आपापल्या जागा बदलल्यानंतर करण डाव्या टोकाकडून 21 वा होतो. तर रांगेत एकूण किती विद्यार्थी आहेत?

डावीकडून 6 वा असणे म्हणजे त्याच्या डावीकडे 5 विद्यार्थी आहेत.
उजवीकडून 22 वा असणे म्हणजे त्याच्या उजवीकडे 21 विद्यार्थी आहेत.
संपूर्ण रांग = डावीकडचे सर्व + स्वतः राहुल + उजवीकडचे सर्व:
एकूण = 5 + 1 + 21 = 27.
नेहमीचे सूत्र म्हणजे एकूण = (डावीकडून स्थान) + (उजवीकडून स्थान) − 1, आणि −1 अशासाठी की राहुल दोन्ही टोकांकडून मोजला जातो.
दोन्ही स्थाने नुसती मिळवल्यास 28 येते, ज्यात तो दोनदा मोजला जातो.

en.text: In a row of 32 students, Sita is 9th from the left end. What is her position from the right end?
en.explanation:
Being 9th from the left means 9 students have been counted up to and including Sita.
That leaves 32 − 9 = 23 students to her right.
Counting from the right end, those 23 students come first and Sita is the very next one.
So her position from the right = 23 + 1 = 24.
The formula is (position from right) = Total − (position from left) + 1. Stopping at 23 forgets to count Sita herself, and that off-by-one is what the question is testing.

mr.text: 32 विद्यार्थ्यांच्या रांगेत सीता डाव्या टोकाकडून 9 वी आहे. तर उजव्या टोकाकडून तिचे स्थान कितवे?
mr.explanation:
डावीकडून 9 वी असणे म्हणजे सीतेसह 9 विद्यार्थी मोजून झाले आहेत.
म्हणजे तिच्या उजवीकडे 32 − 9 = 23 विद्यार्थी उरतात.
उजव्या टोकाकडून मोजायला सुरुवात केल्यास ते 23 विद्यार्थी आधी येतात आणि लगेच सीता येते.
म्हणून उजवीकडून तिचे स्थान = 23 + 1 = 24.
सूत्र: (उजवीकडून स्थान) = एकूण − (डावीकडून स्थान) + 1. 23 वर थांबल्यास स्वतः सीता मोजायची राहून जाते, आणि हीच एका अंकाची चूक प्रश्नात तपासली जाते.

en.text: In a row of students, Karan is 12th from the left end and Meena is 18th from the right end. They interchange their positions, and Karan then becomes 27th from the left end. How many students are there in the row?
en.explanation:
The key idea is that swapping does not move anybody else — Karan simply steps into the exact spot Meena was standing in.
So Meena's original position from the left must have been 27.
We also know Meena was 18th from the right.
Applying the standard rule to Meena: Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1.
Total = 27 + 18 − 1 = 44.
Karan's original position of 12th is not needed at all — it is there to see whether you have understood which person the two facts now describe.

mr.text: एका रांगेत करण डाव्या टोकाकडून 12 वा आहे आणि मीना उजव्या टोकाकडून 18 वी आहे. दोघांनी आपापल्या जागा बदलल्यानंतर करण डाव्या टोकाकडून 27 वा होतो. तर रांगेत एकूण किती विद्यार्थी आहेत?
mr.explanation:
मुख्य मुद्दा असा की जागा बदलल्याने इतर कोणीही हलत नाही — करण नेमका मीना उभी होती त्याच जागी जातो.
म्हणून मीनाचे मूळ स्थान डावीकडून 27 वे असले पाहिजे.
तसेच मीना उजवीकडून 18 वी होती हेही आपल्याला माहीत आहे.
मीनासाठी नेहमीचे सूत्र लावा: एकूण = (डावीकडून स्थान) + (उजवीकडून स्थान) − 1.
एकूण = 27 + 18 − 1 = 44.
करणचे मूळ 12 वे स्थान येथे मुळीच लागत नाही — आता ही दोन्ही माहिती कोणत्या व्यक्तीची आहे हे समजले का, हे तपासण्यासाठीच ते दिले आहे.

Being 20th from the left means there are 19 students to his left.
Being 22th from the right means there are 21 students to his right.

en.text: What is the angle, in degrees, between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 8:30?
en.explanation:
Measure both hands from the 12 mark and then subtract — never try to eyeball it.
The minute hand covers the full 360° in 60 minutes, so it moves 6° per minute. At 30 minutes it is at 30 × 6 = 180° from 12.
The hour hand covers 360° in 12 hours, so it moves 30° per hour AND an extra 0.5° per minute. This half-degree drift is the step almost everyone forgets.
At 8:30 the hour hand is at 8 × 30 + 30 × 0.5 = 240 + 15 = 255° from 12.
Difference = |255 − 180| = 75°.
A clock angle is always reported as the smaller of the two arcs, so the answer is 75°.

mr.text: घड्याळात 8:30 वाजता तास काटा व मिनिट काटा यांच्यातील कोन किती अंश असेल?
